questions.q: Which payment, and for how much, ends up duplicated on the bank's side?
options: Both payments, $27,600.00 combined
Neither payment is duplicated
questions.explain: PMT-21087, the $9,200.00 EFT payment for invoice INV-MER-88290, is the one retransmitted twice by the bank's processor.

questions.q: What causes the duplicate transmission, according to this lesson?
options: Chen Liu submitted the payment process request twice by mistake
Oracle Fusion generated two separate payment records for the same invoice
A network timeout retry on the bank's ACH processor retransmitted the file a second time
Meridian requested a duplicate payment
questions.explain: The payment file transmits once from Oracle Fusion; a network timeout retry on the bank's side causes it to be retransmitted, outside LTV's control.

questions.q: How many times does Oracle Fusion record the PMT-21087 disbursement?
options: Twice, matching the bank's two debits
Once — Oracle Fusion's own records are completely accurate
Zero times, since the payment failed validation
Three times, due to a retry loop in Payables
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion shows exactly one $9,200.00 disbursement for PMT-21087, matching the one validated invoice — the duplication happens entirely outside the system.

questions.q: What accounting entry does each clean payment record in Oracle Fusion?
options: Debit Cash, credit Accounts Payable
Debit Accounts Payable — Trade, credit Cash — Operating
Debit Inventory, credit Accounts Payable
Debit Accrued Liabilities, credit Cash
questions.explain: Each payment debits Accounts Payable — Trade (2110) and credits Cash — Operating (1110).

questions.q: What broader lesson about month-end discrepancies does this lesson draw out?
options: Every discrepancy is caused by a configuration mistake inside Oracle Fusion
Some discrepancies originate outside the system, between the GL and an external source like a bank, not from a system or user error
Supplier payments should never be batched together in one payment process request
EFT payments should be avoided in favor of paper checks
questions.explain: The lesson draws a distinction between an internal configuration or user error and a reconciling item that originates entirely outside the system, like a bank-side duplicate transmission.
